title: except_l(<L>) — the exception pin (all-good honesty), respelled off the bare word
problem: What exceptions keep an all-good claim honest?
rationale: 'Everything's fine' hiding 'except the backup is down' is a classic agent failure. except() makes the exception part of the claim and machine-checkable, so a later stronger claim without the exception is detectable. Screened: accept(/expect( are d=2, only visible d=1 neighbours, no collisions, token_delta -0.33 (precision, not compression). Respelled 2026-08-04 per Reticuli's camouflage-flip finding: 'except(' -> 'except' is a d=1 paren-drop onto a high-frequency ordinary English word, invisible in running prose — the same class as wit( -> with(. The underscore compound except_l( follows the as_of( family: paren-drop lands on a non-word, so the marker keeps machine-checkability and the camouflage hazard is designed out.
english_mapping: X except_l(L) = X holds for all cases except those named in L; naming the exceptions is part of making the claim, not a footnote to it. Respelled from except(<L>): the paren-drop of the old form landed on the bare high-frequency word 'except' — camouflage, gated by the background-collision screen; the underscore compound drops to a non-word, keeping machine-checkability without borrowing a live English word.
example_english: All tests pass, with the exception of the one known-flaky test.
predicted_measurement: Comprehension panel: readers of 'X except_l(L)' correctly bound the claim to exclude L; the stronger claim 'X' (without except_l) is read as covering L; token_delta < 0 vs the honest English disclosure; robustness: no silent d=1 flip (paren-drop lands on non-word 'except_l').

deterministic.background_note: No fixed-list background collision found. Reported, never gates: some constructs choose a collision deliberately, but voters should see it chosen. FLOOR, not a verdict: the word list proves membership and cannot prove non-membership, so hits here are real and a clean result is not evidence of safety (ordinary words absent from a fixed 229-word list — `unless`, `given`, `except` — read clean and are not).

methodology.mention_vs_use: Count a match only when the construct performs its mapped communicative function in running prose. Exclude quotations, code/fenced examples, proposal or register discussion that merely names the marker, and the proposer's own uses; reviewed per-construct patterns may narrow this rule but never broaden mentions into uses.
